style.name: Inflatable
style.description: Glossy inflated vinyl and mirror-foil balloon objects in a bright seamless studio: puffy pillow letters, numbers, arrows, stars, hearts and speech bubbles with a flat welded seam round the edge, pinched scalloped corners, tight wrinkles radiating from the seam, a little valve and strong soft-box highlights. Inflation is a pure function of time: each object starts as a flat, crumpled outline on the floor, its skin is rebuilt every frame from fill(t) — thickness swells from the middle outward, wrinkles tighten and fade, it stands up, overshoots and wobbles to rest with a squeaky stretch. Objects also deflate (sag, fold, sink), bump neighbours and squash on contact, get squeezed so the air shifts to one side, or float up on ribbons and bob. Words inflate letter by letter; air hiss, rubber squeaks and a boing come from the same plan.
motion: Inflate: fill(t) 0 -> 1 rebuilds the skin from the flat outline every frame: thickness = pillow profile (distance-to-edge) times an air front that spreads from the middle outward; crumple and wrinkles fade with fill.
As fill passes ~40 % the object stands up from the floor about its bottom edge, hops, then overshoots: a squeaky vertical stretch, a bulge and a side rock that ring down as a closed-form damped sine.
Words inflate letter by letter (stagger ~0.5 s); each letter's overshoot bumps its left neighbour, which squashes on the contact side and rocks away (planned, not simulated).
Deflate: fill drops fast, the top sags and folds forward, then the whole skin flops backward and sinks flat, wrinkles returning.
Squeeze: the air shifts to one side (one half thins, the other bulges and pushes outward). Float: foil balloons lift on ribbons tied to a weight and bob.
